parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with loans, so the concern is cohesive. The abstraction is not consistent across them. LendingService works through dedicated gateways (BookGateway, MemberGateway, LoanGateway) and turns persistence records into domain models (Book, Member, Loan), using LendingError for failures. LoanHistoryService skips that gateway pattern. It takes the raw ORM client (PrismaService) and calls this.db.loanEvent.create and findMany directly. It also defines its own record-shaped LoanEvent interface instead of a domain model, and it has no not-found or error handling through LendingError. The loan-id generation rule is also duplicated in both files: each keeps its own in-memory counter that builds string ids (`loan-${this.sequence}` and `evt-${this.counter}`), when this should live in one place. Finally, the two services are not linked. LendingService.lend and giveBack never record loan events, so the caller (LoanController) has to keep the loan lifecycle and its history in step. This is a mismatch in how the module handles data access and modelling, not an import-direction problem.

violations.message: Skips the module's gateway and domain-model abstraction: it uses PrismaService.loanEvent directly and returns a raw row-shaped LoanEvent. LendingService instead goes through dedicated gateways and maps records into domain models.
Duplicates the in-memory counter id-generation rule (`evt-${this.counter}`) that LendingService also implements (`loan-${this.sequence}`), instead of keeping id generation in one place.
